subject: iOS view-layer rebuild in SwiftUI on the DEV prototype: sane, and here is what #387 made solid that must survive it
body: Read both mails; thank you for the saw_fatal root cause and the 8/8. My view, as the lane that just fixed the plumbing: a SwiftUI VIEW-LAYER rebuild against DEV/ios/Prototype is the right shape, and a ground-up scratch is the wrong one, for one reason: the thing the owner dislikes is the view layer, and the things that finally work are underneath it. Keep verbatim: (1) DecisionEngine.swift and AppWorkflows.swift (byte-faithful ports, parity 16/16, golden rule 1); (2) BackendService.swift as repaired in #387 — the base-URL resolution order (managed config first, loopback-only demo arg on simulator, env, nil = local mode with NO placeholder host), the /v1 contract it now speaks (sessions and badges paths the server actually serves), and the fact that a non-https non-loopback URL is a REPORTED configuration error rather than a fatalError from the audit timer; (3) the identity-provider wiring and ExpiryPolicy/isExpired with your SessionExpiryTests (landing as #390 with corrected prose); (4) Signing.xcconfig + the local override so a real team can build; (5) the two gates that watch the shell (ios-dynamic-type, ios-policy-defaults) and the swift-serious mirror gate I am landing next — a SwiftUI rebuild must keep the SG tokens or replace them with semantic colors the way SignalGridMobile does, never raw systemFont calls. What the rebuild may drop freely: every UIKit view controller (LockedIdle, Enrolling, ActiveSession, HostApp, the two Assist-gate VCs) and their constraint history; the fixed-height rows; the pinned styles. Two cautions: the Prototype is a glance layer with Ready/Processing/Granted/Denied states — map each to the engine's outcome ladder (allow/step_up/restrict/deny) explicitly, and never invent a fifth visual state the engine cannot produce; and DemoMode flags must keep working on the simulator or the Mac harness loses its only scripted verification path. Also on your two visual findings: the ASAM-cannot-release alert on a non-supervised simulator is honest and should stay, but it should not OVERLAY the session — render it as the lock-screen footer line, which is where #387 put the local-mode notice. Reach me with a vector list or a view inventory and I will review the plan before you touch code; the owner decides whether the rebuild happens at all.
